title: Every secret access lands on an audit sink with metadata and never a value
iWant: a durable per-access audit trail that never carries the secret bytes
soThat: I can answer who read what and when without the log store becoming a secrets store

acceptanceCriteria.description: A successful `get(name)` emits exactly one audit event carrying `name`, `path`, `environment`, `principal`, `outcome: 'served'`, and `at`; no field on the event contains the secret value or any substring of it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process that has authorised the audit sink and holds the value V for logical name `N`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process calls `secretsClient.get('N')` and reads the audit sink for events matching that call
acceptanceCriteria.then: exactly one event is emitted, its keys are the enumerated set above, and byte-equality checks against V return no match on any field value

acceptanceCriteria.description: A refused access emits one audit event with the correct refusal outcome and no value bytes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running process whose declared slice does not include `C`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process calls `secretsClient.get('C')` and the sink is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: one event is emitted with `outcome: 'refusedOutOfSlice'`, name `C`, and no field contains vendor path metadata beyond what the manifest already declares

acceptanceCriteria.description: The audit sink is pluggable through a project-supplied adapter; the blueprint's client uses a stub in-memory sink in tests and a project-supplied sink in production.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process wired against an in-memory audit adapter for tests
acceptanceCriteria.when: the process runs its test suite covering successful and refused fetches
acceptanceCriteria.then: the in-memory adapter accumulates exactly one event per fetch attempt and no vendor SDK is invoked for the audit path
